It is a target of 1,3-dibenzylurea, sufugolix, and cis-isopinocamphone, all of which are known to interact with the hemagglutinin structural subunit. The evidence suggests that the compound may act as a ligand or modulator of the hemagglutinin structural subunit, possibly through a common mechanism involving ion transport or structural interaction. The overlapping targets across different pathways indicate a potential role in the regulation of hemagglutinin function, though the exact mechanism remains to be elucidated. The integration of these findings highlights the compound's potential as a therapeutic agent or inhibitor targeting the hemagglutinin structural subunit.
